Length therefore trades amplitude against localization and prevalence, while positivity trades monotonic selection against sign symmetry.

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Compact frequency support makes the smoothing compatible with positivity: it forgets high coefficients but keeps a uniformly positive block that the resonator can amplify. Time localization and coefficient selection are separately tunable, and the inequality kappa<1-beta is the budget that prevents the longer resonator from leaking into the excluded central region.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: The proof bridges a maximum to a weighted convolution mean, then uses Lemma 1 to bridge that mean to a positive Dirichlet series and an explicit residue. The sinc-squared/triangular Fourier pair supplies coefficient control; the Gaussian supplies off-diagonal and far-tail control.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: The proof chooses a sinc-squared kernel with nonnegative compactly supported triangular Fourier transform, uses second-moment and Gaussian-decay estimates to remove central and far ranges, and requires kappa below one minus beta for error control. Lemma 1 supplies the coefficient series and pole term, Lemmas 5 and 6 control the resonator mean, and the final rescaling adjusts the initially enlarged interval to the theorem's range. The analysis correctly limits the result to existence and records its dependence on the particular kernel and parameter balance.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The proof chooses a sinc-squared K whose Fourier transform is triangular, nonnegative, and supported up to 2 epsilon log T. A second-moment bound for zeta controls the contribution from |t|<=T^beta, rapid Gaussian decay controls |t|>T log T, and N=[T^kappa] with kappa<1-beta controls the resonator error. Lemma 1 rewrites the full convolution as F(t)=sum K-hat(log n)n^{-1/2-it} plus the pole residue. Lemmas 5 and 6 lower-bound the main weighted mean, K-hat stays bounded below on n<=T^epsilon, and a final rescaling of T and slight change of beta restores [T^beta,T].
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The argument proves existence, not prevalence. It first locates a value on an enlarged interval and relies on a final parameter adjustment for the theorem's stated range. The pole estimate, error exponents, and positivity all depend on the particular kernel design. Equations (25)-(28) contain text-layer damage in kernel scaling, powers, and nested logarithms, and the residue argument inherits the sign ambiguity seen in Lemma 1. Verify every exact formula before reuse. Viewing compact frequency support and Gaussian time localization as coordinated but distinct filters is a faithful synthesis of the two kernels used. Kernel scaling, Fourier normalization, residue argument, error powers, interval endpoints, and nested logarithms are formula-sensitive; the residue also inherits the earlier sign ambiguity.
